clue.text: Example of an insect blight

indicators.note: a blight spoils and twists things, so the letters of the words before it are ruined into a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener holds up a ravaged leaf as one case of insect damage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blight' rearranges AN plus INSECT; 'of' just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case or specimen illustrating something, a synonym for an example.

clue.text: Bad spirit is displayed over wildcat strike

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece displayed over another comes above it, so first

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous demon

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters of cat are rearranged

explanation.surface: A demon presides over an unofficial walkout by workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildcat strike' looks like an industrial dispute, but 'wild' rearranges CAT into ACT under IMP.
explanation.definitionFit: An impact is a collision or forcible blow, a synonym for a strike.

clue.text: A Greek character without a casual shirt? Shame!

indicators.note: an old sense of without is outside, so the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: sigma is a letter of the Greek alphabet
a T-shirt is a casual shirt, giving T

explanation.surface: A Greek man with no casual top feels embarrassed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: SIGMA goes round T.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of disgrace attaching to someone, a synonym for shame.

clue.text: She's written several articles

parts.note: the grammatical articles an, the and a, in a row
the grammatical articles an, the and a, in a row
the grammatical articles an, the and a, in a row

explanation.surface: A woman journalist has had a number of pieces published.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' suggests newspaper pieces, but means grammatical articles; Anthea is a girl's name, defined by 'She'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthea is a female first name, so a woman, referred to as she.

clue.text: Switches around many locks when making furniture

indicators.note: one piece placed around others encloses them

parts.note: canes are switches, thin flexible sticks
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
locks are tresses of hair

explanation.surface: A hairdresser uses sticks round lots of tresses while building chairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals the container; 'when making' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cane chairs are seats woven from rattan or cane, items of furniture.

clue.text: Injured man had to carry a gun

indicators.note: one piece carrying another holds it within, so the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: 'he had' contracts to HE'D, the man having had
an arm is a weapon, a gun

explanation.surface: A man who carried a firearm got hurt, as in a crime report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man had' has to be read as a contraction of 'he had'; 'to carry' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmed is a past participle meaning hurt or damaged, a straight synonym for injured.

clue.text: For a seaman to offend a social worker is unusual

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
to err is to sin or offend
an ant is a social insect and a worker

explanation.surface: A sailor insulting a welfare officer is out of the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' sounds like a welfare job, but it is an ant, a social insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberrant means departing from the normal course, a synonym for unusual.

clue.text: Declare support

explanation.definitionFit: To maintain is to assert something as true, and also to keep up or support financially.

clue.text: Catastrophe as a result of underworld bloomer

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the underworld itself
an aster is a flower, something that blooms

explanation.surface: A disaster caused by a hellish blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' is British slang for a blunder, which fits the surface, but here means a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster is a sudden calamity, a synonym for catastrophe.

clue.text: Indicating renovation to the brickwork

explanation.definitionFit: Pointing means showing with a finger, and also the repair of mortar joints between bricks.

clue.text: Thoughtless and really friendless girl

indicators.note: 'friend-less' tells us to drop a word for friend from the word before it

parts.note: an ally is a friend
Miss is the title of an unmarried girl

explanation.surface: A careless young woman is described as having no friends at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'friendless' as 'friend-less': the word for a friend is removed from 'really'.
explanation.definitionFit: Remiss means negligent or careless in one's duty, close to thoughtless.

clue.text: Force holding thousands means business

indicators.note: one word holding another contains it, so the second piece sits within the first

parts.note: to coerce is to force someone
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Using compulsion while gripping large sums of money is what trade is about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' signals the container; 'means' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Commerce is the buying and selling of goods, a synonym for business or trade.

clue.text: Records of western ceremonies

parts.note: rites are ceremonies

explanation.surface: Documents describing the rituals of the American West.
explanation.definitionFit: To record is to put down in writing, so the verb records means writes.

clue.text: Low-level illumination turned up overmuch in air travel

indicators.note: one piece sitting in another goes inside it

parts.note: flights are journeys by air

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: too means excessively, overmuch

explanation.surface: Lights on planes have been turned up far too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses TOO to OOT, which goes 'in' FLIGHTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Footlights are the row of lamps along the front of a stage floor, lighting from low down.

clue.text: Dressing many a one is awkward

indicators.note: something awkward is clumsy and out of shape, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Getting dressed is clumsy for plenty of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing' seems to be about clothes, but it is a salad dressing; 'awkward' rearranges MANY A ONE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayonnaise is a thick egg and oil sauce served as a salad dressing.

clue.text: A partiality for quiet charm

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
to enchant is to charm

explanation.surface: A fondness for gentle charm.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a strong liking or inclination, a synonym for a partiality.

clue.text: Member of the family presenting an account

explanation.definitionFit: A relation is a relative, and also the telling or narration of a story, an account.

clue.text: Never to name it could be wrong

indicators.note: the letters could be put in the wrong order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice never to name something, in case you get it wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be wrong' rearranges TO NAME IT.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means on no occasion whatever, an idiom equivalent to never.

clue.text: Those not in the minority choose to speak out

parts.note: to elect is to choose by vote
to orate is to speak out formally

explanation.surface: The majority get to pick their spokesperson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minority' here means being under age: those not minors are the people entitled to vote.
explanation.definitionFit: The electorate are the adult voters, those past their minority, or legal childhood.

clue.text: Issue some schemer generally raises

indicators.note: some of the words means part of their letters, run together

explanation.surface: A plotter usually brings up an awkward problem.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'schemer generally'; 'raises' is surface padding linking it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue is to come out or flow forth, a synonym for emerge.

clue.text: Fussy academic's huff about a newspaper leader

indicators.note: one piece about another surrounds it

parts.note: to huff is to puff or pant
an ed, editor, leads a newspaper

explanation.surface: A scholar takes offence over a newspaper's editorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'huff' suggests a sulk, but it is a breath, PANT; 'leader' is not the editorial but the editor, ED.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedant is someone overly concerned with minor rules and details, especially in learning.

clue.text: To send for change is a Continental resort

indicators.note: the letters are put up for change, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions to post a letter for altering, at a European seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for change' rearranges TO SEND; Ostend is a Belgian seaside port.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostend is a seaside town on the Belgian coast, a resort on the Continent.

clue.text: Note synthetic stuff's colour

parts.note: C is a musical note
rayon is a synthetic fabric, the 's standing for 'is'

explanation.surface: The hue of an artificial fabric is noted.
explanation.definitionFit: To crayon is to colour in with wax sticks, so the verb matches colour.

clue.text: Company head showing great determination

parts.note: a firm is a business company
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A company boss displays strong resolve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' suggests a boss, but it is a headland, NESS, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Firmness is resolute steadiness of purpose, a synonym for great determination.

clue.text: Put a body of police in charge — sharp!

parts.note: the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the British detective branch

explanation.surface: An order to put detectives in command, delivered briskly.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidic means sour-tasting or cutting, and both senses fit sharp.

clue.text: Deficit for a wee while

parts.note: wee, Scottish for small, means short
an age is a long while

explanation.surface: A small debt to tide someone over for a little time.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortage is a lack or shortfall, an amount less than needed, a synonym for deficit.

clue.text: Private transport that must be shared

definitions.text: Private transport that must be shared

parts.words: Private transport that must be shared
parts.note: a personal vehicle that, oddly, needs two riders: a bicycle built for two

explanation.surface: A paradox of one's own vehicle that needs company.
explanation.definitionFit: A tandem is a bicycle for two riders, private transport that can only be used shared.

clue.text: A dessert may well be insisted upon

indicators.note: suggests the letters could well become something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A diner demands a pudding after dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Asserted means stated forcefully, so a point asserted is one insisted upon.
